elements.evidence: The rendered Section 15.16 still binds both Parties: "Neither Party shall ... solicit such employee to terminate his or her employment ...". Customer (PB) therefore remains subject to a non-solicit, so the preferred no-restriction outcome is not achieved.
Rendered text opens "Neither Party shall ..." and the carve-out refers to "the Parties' right", so the obligation runs symmetrically against Vendor and Customer.

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Scope is limited to "an employee of the other Party ... involved in the performance or oversight of any of the development activities hereunder"; it does not extend to all personnel.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: The Term-plus-[***] tail is deleted and replaced with "until twelve (12) months after an employee of the other Party ceases to be involved in the performance or oversight of any of the development activities hereunder" — the temporal anchor is the end of the individual's involvement and the period is exactly 12 months.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Retained sentence: "nothing herein shall restrict or preclude the Parties' right to make generalized searches for employees by way of a general solicitation for employment placed in a trade journal, newspaper or website".

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Added to the same carve-out sentence: "or to hire any employee who approaches a Party on an unsolicited basis", which removes unsolicited-approach hires from the prohibition.

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The operative prohibition is solicitation-only ("shall not ... solicit such employee to terminate his or her employment and accept employment or work as a consultant"); no "employ", "engage" or no-hire language appears, and the carve-out affirmatively preserves the right "to hire".

reasons: Fallback level is complete: all six atomic elements are met in the operative rendered text (mutuality, involvement-limited scope, 12-month post-involvement duration, general-advertisement carve-out, unsolicited-approach carve-out, solicitation-only with no no-hire).
Preferred level is not met and cannot be reached by this redline because the mutual non-solicit binding Customer is retained; that is acceptable since only one complete level is required.

Deviation classification is correct on the original: the clause ran "During the Term and for a period of [***] thereafter" (an undisclosed, potentially >24-month tail anchored to expiry rather than to the individual's involvement) and contained no unsolicited-approach carve-out — two material fallback failures.

Minimality holds: only two changes were made — the temporal anchor was re-cut to 12 months from the end of involvement (which necessitated moving "is or has been involved" into the "ceases to be involved" formulation) and a short unsolicited-approach clause was appended to the existing carve-out sentence. No survival tail, expense language, remedies, procedures or extra covenants were added, and the favourable general-solicitation carve-out and solicitation-only structure were retained verbatim.

Intent preserved: no defined term, cross-reference or commercial mechanic is disturbed. Deletion of the reference to "the Term" leaves no dangling reference, since "Term" remains defined in Section 14.1 and used elsewhere, and the clause no longer needs it once duration is anchored to individual involvement.

Drafting note (non-blocking): the unsolicited carve-out is expressed as a right "to hire" rather than a right to respond to or negotiate with an unsolicited approacher. This is the customary formulation and suffices against a solicitation-only prohibition, but if the counterparty pushes back, "to hire, or discuss employment with, any employee who approaches a Party on an unsolicited basis" would close the residual argument that pre-hire discussions constitute solicitation.
